research_question: Does the exact first-ten-second Binance futures order imbalance at quarter-hour boundaries, routed by either recent boundary-flow persistence or a separately observed public trend/volume state and confirmed by a later five-minute bar, produce cost-positive four-to-eight-hour directional opportunities?

external_mechanism.source: Kim and Hansen (2026), The Quarter-Hour Effect
reused: first ten seconds of every 15-minute boundary
public price-volume state as a separate explanatory component
adapted: Binance futures one-second klines reconstruct ten-second signed quote-volume imbalance
separate five-minute confirmation creates a new tradable auction leg
one global causal episode across BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP
not_used: current event outcome in threshold selection
realized future funding as a signal

data.context_and_outcome_source: Binance Vision USD-M monthly and daily 1m klines
data.visibility: ten-second boundary state and public context are complete before the separately completed five-minute confirmation interval

evaluation.same_event_arbitration: largest normalized ten-second imbalance times fixed route-quality score, then symbol
evaluation.overlap_policy: no selected episode while the active fixed route horizon is open

advance_gate.final_integrated_system_frequency_requir: at least one independent completed trade per evaluation calendar day after global arbitration

decision_contract.advance: Only a fixed route positive in every declared split and passing the integrated gates advances to a frozen NautilusTrader implementation.
decision_contract.reject: Do not tune ten-second imbalance or state thresholds after evaluation. Preserve only any cross-split-positive route and move to another independent mechanism.
